# BaseHTTPMiddleware doesn't properly handle streaming request bodies

Description

When using BaseHTTPMiddleware with streaming request bodies, the middleware doesn't properly consume the entire request body stream. This causes issues when the client sends data in chunks with the "more_body" flag set.

I've noticed that in some cases, when a client sends a large request body in multiple chunks, the middleware stops processing the request body prematurely, which leads to unexpected behavior in the application.

To reproduce this issue:

```python
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.routing import Route

class CustomMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):
        # Try to access the request body
        body = await request.body()
        print(f"Middleware received body: {body}")
        
        # Continue processing
        response = await call_next(request)
        return response

async def homepage(request):
    # Try to access the request body again
    body = await request.body()
    print(f"View received body: {body}")
    return JSONResponse({"message": "Hello World"})

app = Starlette(
    routes=[Route("/", homepage, methods=["POST"])],
    middleware=[CustomMiddleware()]
)
```

When sending a large request body in chunks, the middleware doesn't fully consume the stream, causing the view function to receive incomplete data or no data at all.

This seems to be related to how the middleware handles the "more_body" flag in streaming request bodies.
